text:
maria: quick heads-up, ran the three-region latency sweep this morning. p50s are close, but p95 in us-west is consistently ~35-60ms higher vs eu-west and us-east on h100-int8 :thinking_face:
kevin: good catch — is that after KV cache warmups?
maria: yes; we waited 60s and ran 1k short-chat requests (seq len ~128). warmups applied.
dana: any difference between the kernel selection on the two regions? we rolled a new kernel build to eu-west last week.
maria: eu-west has kernel v2.4.3 (opt_fused_attention), us-west still on v2.3.9 (fallback path). that maps to a ~20ms gap, but the extra 15-40ms looks like routing fanout + proxy hops.
sam: can you paste the raw p50/p95 numbers?
maria: sure — summary from load test tool:

```
region   gpu    p50(ms)  p95(ms)  qps
us-east  h100   48       118      180
us-west  h100   52       160      175
eu-west  h100   50       120      170
us-west  a100   68       195      150
```

maria: note how us-west p95 spikes on h100 even though p50 is similar to others.
leo: looks like p95 tail only on production routing for us-west? dev cluster same kernel but no tail?
maria: yes, dev-usw is flat. prod-usw uses edge fanout=3 for redundancy — that seems to add variance when one backend is slightly slower.
kevin: hypothesis: fanout increases p95 because we wait for the slowest backend to reply in our current aggregator logic. we should fallback-to-first-success for latency-critical routes.
dana: that would change correctness for streaming responses unless we properly cancel the late answers. we need a safe cancellation token path.
ops-bot: deploy canary scheduled: routing-proxy v1.8.1 -> v1.8.2 on prod-usw at 11:20 UTC :white_check_mark:
maria: for the canary I also tried forcing kernel v2.4.3 on a subset of hosts in prod-usw — p95 dropped ~18ms but still above eu-west.
sam: what about batching config? us-west sees slightly larger batch sizes during peak, could escalate tail latency.
maria: we captured batch stats: avg batch size 3.1 in us-west vs 2.7 in eu-west during test window. changing max_batch_delay to 5ms brought p95 down ~10ms locally.
kevin: two levers then: (1) push kernel v2.4.3 to prod-usw, (2) change aggregator behavior to accept first-success or implement faster cancellation. also tweak batching.
leo: don't forget warmup fragility on int8 quant. sometimes first few requests after cache eviction spike a lot. are cache hit rates similar?
maria: cache hit ~94% across regions; us-west had a short period with 70% earlier in test before warmup completed (we omitted early samples from summary).
dana: can we do a synthetic experiment: route 50% traffic to single-backend (no fanout) vs fanout=3, measure p50/p95? if fanout is the dominant cause that should be obvious.
kevin: +1. also try a variant of aggregator that returns first-success while cancelling others. we have cancel token in runtime — just need config toggle.
ops-bot: test job queued: regional-routing/fanout-ablation-237812 — will run 10k requests per region, 60s warmup, output to s3://redwood-bench/2378123456.json
maria: attaching quick config diff I used locally:

```
routing:
  fanout: 3        # prod-usw default
  aggregator: wait_all  # try: first_success
  cancel_timeout_ms: 20
```

maria: after flipping aggregator->first_success in a local canary (50 hosts), p95 in prod-usw dropped from 160ms -> 125ms (still ~5ms above eu-west).
sam: nice. do we observe any correctness anomalies (message truncation, duplicate events)?
maria: in our canary none observed, but we need broader validation for streaming sessions.
kevin: next steps I propose:
- rollout kernel v2.4.3 to remaining prod-usw hosts (canary first)
- enable aggregator:first_success behind feature flag and stress test
- reduce max_batch_delay by 2ms for h100 pools in us-west
- run fanout ablation job (ops-bot job) and compare tail distributions

dana: add an eval set of 200 prompts to ensure quality/regression after int8 and kernel changes. post results to #eng-ml with perf+quality table.
maria: will do. I'll also include per-route cost delta (tokens/sec and GPU utilization) — initial runs show negligible cost change for first_success.
kevin: excellent. if the fanout is the real culprit we should keep fanout for durability on non-latency routes but switch critical routes to single path with fallback.
leo: fyi, long-term we should consider smarter routing that weights responses by backlog and kernel version — avoid slow replicas for latency SLOs.
maria: noted. I'll post the ops-bot job link + raw artifacts when ready. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
infra-bot: artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/2378123456.json (10.2MB)
maria: thread closed for now, will reopen with results.
